purpose: Keep product specifications, semantic models, implementation plans, and historical handoffs understandable to future contributors and agents by assigning each a precise authority and correcting confirmed current-state drift.
scope: Documentation authority policy, status metadata, link routing, and the confirmed stale claims in design and semantic-model documents. This track establishes maintenance rules without rewriting repository history.
non_goals: Deleting historical handoffs, plans, or Git history.
Claiming that a plan is normative product behavior after code and specification have changed.
Creating a second prose copy of every normative requirement.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A concise authority index at .claude/specs/INDEX.md states that accepted .claude/specs artifacts are top-level normative requirements (they do not require a separate REQ-* file); docs/01-spec.md is normative only where it explicitly says so; docs/00-design.md explains rationale; semantic models describe verified current implementation; plans describe intended work and status; handoffs are historical context. It specifies the conflict-resolution and correction path. Existing dangling linked_requirement fields are a repository-wide migration concern and are not created by this track.

Every new or materially revised specification identifies status, last_verified_revision, owner_track, explicit dependencies, and its relevant implementation plan once one exists. Completed or superseded plans visibly link back to the normative specification rather than presenting themselves as current truth. This metadata is required in the spec itself, not inferred from filename or Git history.

Confirmed stale current-state claims are corrected in the authoritative/current-description location: the design document's shipped-language posture, the semantic version-flow changeset staging behavior, and the semantic error-taxonomy PackageSetMatchedNothing emission behavior. Each correction is validated against the referenced implementation and does not erase historical rationale.

A lightweight documentation check, runnable through the project task runner, applies only to documents designated as current-description material: docs/00-design.md and .claude/semantic-model/*.md. It rejects a newly added assertion matching the documented current-behavior marker unless the same section contains verified_revision or an explicit link to an accepted spec/current implementation. It reports rather than rewrites legacy material and explicitly excludes .claude/specs/, .claude/plans/, handoffs, and historical sections from enforcement.
